learning_outcomes.text: Basic knowledge of production and manufacturing systems.

Ability to draft, sign, and develop projects in the field of mechanical engineering whose purpose is the construction, renovation, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly, or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical and electronic installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing and automation processes.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and aptitudes in the field of mechanical engineering.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Ability to exercise their profession with a cooperative and participatory attitude, and with social responsibility.

To be able, through arguments or procedures developed and supported by themselves, to apply their knowledge, understanding of it, and problem-solving abilities in complex or professional and specialized work environments that require the use of creative and innovative ideas.

To have the ability to collect and interpret data and information on which to base their conclusions, including, when necessary and relevant, reflection on social, scientific, or ethical issues in their field of study.
To know how to communicate clearly and precisely to all types of audiences (specialized or not) knowledge, methodologies, ideas, problems, and solutions in the field of their study.

To be able to identify their own training needs in their field of study and work or professional environment and to organize their own learning with a high degree of autonomy in all types of contexts (structured or unstructured).

Knowledge and understanding: Knowledge and understanding of the engineering disciplines specific to their specialty, at the level necessary to acquire the rest of the degree's competences, including notions of the latest advances.
Knowledge and understanding: Be aware of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.

Engineering analysis: The ability to analyze complex products, processes, and systems in their field of study; select and apply established analytical, calculation, and experimental methods appropriately and correctly interpret the results of such analyses.

Engineering projects: Ability to project, design and develop complex products (parts, components, finished products, etc.), processes and systems of their specialty, that comply with established requirements, including being aware of social, health and safety, environmental, economic and industrial aspects; as well as selecting and applying appropriate design methods.
Practical application of engineering: Understanding of applicable techniques and methods of analysis, design and research and their limitations in their field of expertise.
Practical application of engineering: Knowledge of the application of materials, equipment and tools, technology and engineering processes and their limitations in their field of expertise.
Judgment formation: Ability to manage complex technical or professional activities or projects in their specialty, taking responsibility for decision-making.
Communication and Teamwork: Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems and solutions in the field of engineering and with society in general.

Communication and Teamwork: Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams, and to cooperate with engineers as well as people from other disciplines.
Makes decisions and evaluates the possible consequences of the selected alternative.
Identifies machinery, utilities, tools, and working parameters of various manufacturing processes.
Defines the problem, the development of the solution, as well as the conclusions effectively, and making correct use of language, in writing.
Identify the main manufacturing process for a given part.
Defines the problem, the development of the solution, as well as the conclusions effectively, and making correct use of language orally.
Be able to design manufacturing processes for specific parts, combining technological and economic criteria.
Coordinates their work with other team members, contributes to their team in the development of tasks to be carried out and the creation of a good working environment.

teaching_methods: Project/Problem-Based Learning (development, drafting, presentation of reports/audiovisual material)
Exercise and problem solving (individual and team)
Laboratory and workshop practicals (individual and team)

assessment_methods.method: Project/PBL evaluation (technical capacity, involvement, work, results, documentation, presentation, defense)
Reports on exercises, case studies, computer, simulation, and laboratory practices

assessment_rules: Assessment of project/PBL components is continuous, based on team meetings. A week before final report submission, work is reviewed for improvements; the corrected final report serves as a resit. Individual written and oral tests are used for other technical competences, with re-examinations available. For certain competences, a combination of project work, reports, and individual tests is used, with similar resit provisions for each component.
